findings.evidence: packages/app-backend/src/file-read.ts:59 opens a FileHandle before constructing a highWaterMark:0 response body; cleanup is only in pull/cancel. downloadFile receives Headers rather than a Request/AbortSignal. packages/app-backend/src/runtime.ts close only aborts state.streams (SSE controllers), never these download handles.
findings.refutation: A normally consumed or explicitly cancelled body closes the handle. highWaterMark:0 means a response that is never consumed never enters pull, and the code has no finite lifetime, request-abort callback or runtime-close registry for that case. Garbage collection is not a bounded resource policy.
findings.suggestion: Track downloads with bounded capacity/lifetime and connect request abort, response cancel and runtime shutdown to idempotent descriptor closure; test an unread response.

findings.evidence: packages/app-backend/src/file-write.ts:26-29 reads upload state and creates bytes after the reservation transaction is finished. deleteFile at lines104-109 tombstones, tolerates ENOENT and clears cleanupPending. packages/app-backend/src/store.ts:21-27 supplies only an instance-local promise lane, and PostgreSQL mode accepts multiple pools without an exclusive runtime lock.
findings.refutation: The app_scope row lock correctly serializes quota reservation transactions, and one runtime's exclusive lane serializes local handlers. It does not cover two runtimes: A commits and reads uploading row, pauses before wx; B tombstones the row, unlinks absent bytes and clears cleanupPending; A resumes wx create. A leaves an orphan physical file while metadata no longer reserves its bytes. The scope marker allows the same cell to reopen the root and supplies no process lock.
findings.suggestion: Enforce one active runtime per application store AND filesystem identity, or serialize physical creation/deletion and durable intent settlement across runtimes. State the supported concurrency contract explicitly.

findings.evidence: packages/app-backend/src/store.ts:41-50 caches app_scope.recoveryHold only at open. packages/app-backend/src/state.ts:48-51 tests this mutable in-memory flag without reading persisted hold. A targeted reference check shows recovery.ts:105-107 persists hold and updates only its own ApplicationStore object.
findings.refutation: Shared external lifecycle unavailability blocks ordinary work during import if every process sees it. Persistent recovery hold exists precisely to keep a restored destination denied even if lifecycle later says available. Another already-open runtime retains recoveryHeld=false; enabling external lifecycle then bypasses the persisted hold. No duplicate-runtime prohibition currently prevents this interleaving.
findings.suggestion: Read persisted recovery hold live in authority checks, including within serialized mutations, or explicitly deny additional runtimes using a durable process/session lock. Keep held destinations denied independently of lifecycle availability.

findings.evidence: packages/app-backend/src/file-write.ts:58 ignores FileHandle.write's bytesWritten result before syncing and advancing metadata. Lines59-63 only reconcile physical size equal to old offset or the complete chunk end; an interrupted write leaving a partial tail always fails the same exact retry with UPLOAD_UNCERTAIN.
findings.refutation: Normal local writes commonly complete in one call, and completeFile later checks physical length. Neither proves a full acknowledged chunk: the API can acknowledge full offset after a short successful write, and a crash during write can leave an intermediate size for which no resume/reconcile path exists. Keeping the upload uncommitted protects readers but does not satisfy interrupt/resume behavior.
findings.suggestion: Loop until all bytes are written and synced, and reconcile a partial tail using the retained exact chunk intent before allowing metadata advancement. Add deterministic short-write and restart-with-partial-tail cases.

passed_observations: Exact canonical origins, loopback-only cleartext, rejected wildcard hosts, listener-fixed cell scope and version checking are present.
Application session material is cell-derived and lives in independent auth tables; JSON token fields are stripped and caller privilege fields are rejected.
File reservation and exact pending chunk identities now commit before filesystem mutation; uncertain bytes and cleanup pending rows retain quota.
File names never select physical paths; hardlink/symlink checks, owner-scoped database lookups and opened descriptor identity checks are present.
Download delivery validates session, grant expiry/revocation, lifecycle epoch and committed ownership before and after each read.
SSE is pull-driven with zero prefetch, one bounded event at a time, per-user signed cursor, current-session/lifecycle validation and explicit gap/refetch behavior.
Unread SSE responses now release stream capacity through a finite lifetime timer; disconnect/cancel/shutdown participate in controller cleanup.
